records.region: Northern drainage of central Cuba, through the Ciego de Ávila lowlands into the northern coastal wetland and shallow coastal sea.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected southern opening and the required northwest-to-north connection across the flat vegetated/agricultural plain, spanning original parts0–2, are not established at useful ordinary corridor scale. The overview and one enlarged original show the setting, but patchy cloud/shadow and undifferentiated low-relief cover do not expose a definite continuous receiving corridor for that interval. Basin-level prose and the study’s small regional diagram cannot close this specific link. This is not a demand for exact banks or continuously wet water. Specifically, the images do not distinguish which northgoing lowland/collector receives the selected southern starting area through the intervening cloudy and cultivated terrain. They show a broad plain, but not an identifiable common receiving depression for this required transfer. A proven common lowland with only an invisible narrow channel would have been sufficient; that positive receiving relationship is what remains missing.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No complete representative river identity is established. La Yana is directly documented as a drainage-basin name and Canal La Yana as a managed-channel label in the institutional study. Neither is extended across the entire selected upper plain, wetlands and coastal terminal.
records.completion_scope: Bounded pass complete. All20 stored parts were considered. Middle lowland/wetland continuity, the lower coastal wetland corridor and both actual terminal descriptions are supported at ordinary terrain scale. The required southern connection remains unestablished, so there is one material-pending state rather than completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: No complete representative river identity is established. La Yana is directly documented as a drainage-basin name and Canal La Yana as a managed-channel label in the institutional study. Neither is extended across the entire selected upper plain, wetlands and coastal terminal.

scope_limits: The whole natural-river name remains unsupported; basin and managed-channel terminology is kept in bounded observations only.
No claim that the selected lower route crosses the whole open Laguna La Redonda or follows the separate La Redonda–La Leche transfer.
Cloud/shadow and low-relief cover leave the required southern connection unresolved; generalized selected shape alone is not proof.
Source and rendered endings are treated separately, without adopting either as a precise contemporary surveyed shoreline crossing.
Historic cartographic access/use restrictions remain unchanged; new successful photographs do not release those publications.

records.region: Bering glacier region, Robinson Mountains and Duktoth coastal receiving corridor
records.candidate_name_role: No supported representative name for the entire selection; component names are confined to bounded_name_observations.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected part leaves the small southern ice-margin lake and descends toward a separately mapped tributary below. The detailed National Map original depicts the lake, intervening rock/snow-covered slope and the lower feeder without establishing their through-transfer. The independent narrow image shows lakes, snow-covered relief and the receiving slope but does not resolve the ordinary outlet connection. Proximity and modeled continuity alone are insufficient. This is the single material correspondence gap.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chosen upper ice-field passage, southern glacier-margin lake setting, separate western feeder valley, Duktoth River receiving corridor and actual coastal ending were reviewed. One short transfer from the selected small southern ice-margin lake to the mapped feeder below remains unestablished. The successful narrow imagery view is snow-covered and does not establish that ordinary outlet connection. This is one source-material-pending state; Duktoth River is retained only for the mapped receiving and lower river.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass finished after two original National Map views and one independent narrow photographic view. All selected parts were reviewed, but the short lake/glacier-margin-to-feeder transfer prevents whole-feature correspondence completion. The gap is not a demand for a precise present ice front or subglacial hydraulic route.
records.supported_name_scope: The chosen upper ice-field passage, southern glacier-margin lake setting, separate western feeder valley, Duktoth River receiving corridor and actual coastal ending were reviewed. One short transfer from the selected small southern ice-margin lake to the mapped feeder below remains unestablished. The successful narrow imagery view is snow-covered and does not establish that ordinary outlet connection. This is one source-material-pending state; Duktoth River is retained only for the mapped receiving and lower river.

scope_limits: The single unresolved ordinary geographic transfer is the small southern glacier-margin lake to the feeder below, centered on FID2725 stored part29. This is not proof of disconnection; available material does not establish the through-link.
Upper modeled positions traverse glacier ice. Ordinary ice-field correspondence does not establish one natural river, current ice hydraulics or a precisely named glacier boundary for each upper arm.
Additional small glacier labels in the overview were not reliably transcribed and are not promoted into candidate names.
The lake/ice geometry and the photographic snow cover may represent different dates. No current ice-front, water-level or discharge claim is made.
The source and rendered terminal positions are different placements within the same coastal receiving neighborhood, not a correction to the preserved geometry.
No formal name-register record, whole-feature natural-river name or Korean rendering was verified.

records.region: Southern Oregon and northern California, United States
records.candidate_name_role: Representative downstream receiving-system identity for the researched composite.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected headward Chrome Creek corridor and North Fork Smith River join the main Smith River corridor, which continues through the lower river to its coastal estuarine receiving setting. Smith River is supported as a representative receiving identity; it does not rename the separately labeled creek, fork or coastal extension.
records.completion_scope: Both selected mainstem fragments and all 32 stored parts have ordinary geographic correspondence from the Chrome Creek opening through North Fork Smith and the main Smith River to the distinct source/render coastal settings. Smith River is the representative receiving-system name; fork and creek names remain bounded.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected headward Chrome Creek corridor and North Fork Smith River join the main Smith River corridor, which continues through the lower river to its coastal estuarine receiving setting. Smith River is supported as a representative receiving identity; it does not rename the separately labeled creek, fork or coastal extension.

scope_limits: Smith River is a representative receiving-system identity. The full composite also includes a separately named headward creek and fork, so no whole-feature scalar name is asserted.

The exact first position of the Chrome Creek name and the precise legal fork/mainstem name-transition vertices are unverified. Continuous creek and receiving-valley correspondence is established at ordinary geographic scale.

Source and render endpoints are distinct. The source is in the estuarine setting; the rendered endpoint is at its western ocean-side margin. Neither is promoted to the exact contemporary outlet throat.
The source is generalized composite cartography with unestablished contributing epochs, not current-flow, exact-bank or authoritative registry evidence.

An optional headward detail acquisition was cancelled before its terminal result could be confirmed. Its outputs are excluded; the previously completed and actually read overview independently suffices for the bounded conclusion.

records.region: Yakutat glacier field, Harlequin Lake and Dangerous River coastal plain
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-system identity; not a uniform name for every glacier or lake component.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected continuous glacier–Harlequin Lake–western outlet–Dangerous River–coast composite is represented by its directly labeled receiving river. Harlequin Lake and glacier components keep their separate bounded identities.
records.completion_scope: Complete ordinary glacier/lake/river/receiving-shore correspondence and supported representative Dangerous River identity. No further acquisition is needed for this bounded pass. No uniform natural-river name for the ice-field and lake components is asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: The selected continuous glacier–Harlequin Lake–western outlet–Dangerous River–coast composite is represented by its directly labeled receiving river. Harlequin Lake and glacier components keep their separate bounded identities.

scope_limits: The map supports ordinary geographic continuity through the upper ice field, not an identified surface or subglacial river. Precise present ice-front positions and hydraulics are unverified and unnecessary for this result.

Dangerous River is supported as the representative receiving river for the fully traced composite, while its name is not asserted to be the uniform natural-river name of the chosen upper glacier or Harlequin Lake.
The lake label and lake-spanning river text belong to one cartographic compilation; they are not independent naming authorities.
Source and rendered coastal endpoints differ and are separately described, without a claim that either matches today's active mouth or tide line.
No formal name-register verification or Korean rendering was completed.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
